prompt: Every push automatically builds the code and runs all the tests.
why: Building and testing automatically on every push is continuous integration. It catches problems minutes after they're made, not days later.
trap: The tests are units; running them on every push is CI.

prompt: A red X appears on the pull request because the build failed on the server.
tells: the build failed on the server
why: The build ran on a server, not your laptop, and failed. That red mark is a continuous integration check reporting a failure.
trap: Conflicts come from git, not the build.

prompt: Nobody can merge until the automated checks pass.
why: Automated checks must pass before anyone can merge. Continuous integration acts as a gate that keeps main working.

prompt: It worked on her laptop, but the shared build machine catches a missing dependency.
why: Her laptop had a dependency installed that the project didn't declare. A clean shared build machine catches that, which is one reason for CI.
trap: Staging is for trying the app, not building it.

prompt: A pipeline lints, tests and builds each change.
tells: A pipeline lints, tests and builds
why: Linting, testing and building every change automatically, in order, is a CI pipeline.

prompt: Small changes are merged into main several times a day, each checked by automation.
why: Merging small changes often, each one checked by automation, is the practice continuous integration is named after.
trap: Flags may help, but the habit is CI.
